title: Create reproducible multi-platform release pipeline
notes: MBR-903 ORCHESTRATES RightKit; it does not reimplement building, signing, or sealing. RightKit already owns, end to end via apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs and package.json's release:doctor/release:build:mac/release:build:win scripts: tauri build, codesign+notarize+staple (mac, MBR-901), Azure Artifact Signing (Windows, MBR-902), RightKit's own hardeningscan.mjs, and sealing a schema:1 release-manifest.json under .right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<shortcommit>/{mac,windows}/ (tools/rightkit/packages/release/build-release.mjs's sealRelease(), release-state.mjs's runBuildStateMachine()). This task adds a layer above that RightKit already does not provide: cross-platform release IDENTITY binding (does the exact same commit sit behind BOTH the macOS and the Windows sealed output?) and PROOF that identity is reproducible and that drift is caught, not silently accepted.

What this task added, all new, under scripts/release/pipeline/ (a new subdirectory, per this task's allowed paths): identity.mjs (computeReleaseGeneration -- a deterministic sha256 over product+CRYPT_VECTOR_DISPATCH_V2+commit+tree+version+ordered target set; resolveGitSourceIdentity -- read-only git rev-parse/status, never mutating); platform-targets.mjs (maps the four logical targets in the pre-existing release/contracts/platforms.v1.json onto the RightKit platform directory that actually produces each, honestly marking mac-x64 and windows-arm64 as not-buildable/conformance-only today rather than fabricating support apps/membrane-hub's config does not have); sealed-platforms.mjs (reads whatever RightKit has already sealed for one target, by REUSING scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs's sealedReleaseDir/readSealedReleaseManifest/verifySealedInstallerHash (MBR-901) and scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs's validateSealedManifest (MBR-902) -- imported, never duplicated -- and fails closed with a new ReleaseDriftError when a sealed manifest's own commit does not match the release's resolved commit); multi-platform-release.mjs (the CLI/library entry point: builds the combined plan across all four targets, and writes an immutable evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json -- write-once per releaseId, idempotent for an unchanged plan, throws ImmutableReleaseConflictError on drift).

Reproducibility is demonstrated, not asserted: pipeline.test.mjs proves (1) computeReleaseGeneration returns a byte-identical digest across two independent calls with identical inputs, and a different digest when only `tree` changes; (2) buildMultiPlatformPlan called twice with identical inputs produces a deep-equal plan (assert.deepEqual on the whole object, including release_generation and every target's status); (3) writeImmutableReleaseGeneration writing the same plan twice is a no-op (written:false, same path, same bytes on disk) -- this is what running the orchestrator once on the Mac and again after the Windows build looks like for a release that has not drifted.

Drift being caught is demonstrated, not asserted: three tests construct a sealed release-manifest.json that lives at the expected release's releaseId-derived path but whose own recorded `commit` field names a DIFFERENT commit -- the exact shape of 'the Windows machine built before pulling the Mac's commit,' which is Adrian's real two-machine workflow's actual failure mode. readSealedPlatformStage throws ReleaseDriftError (asserted via error.detail.expectedCommit/sealedCommit); buildMultiPlatformPlan (which calls it once per target) propagates that failure rather than silently combining a COMMIT_A mac stage with a COMMIT_B windows stage into one release; and writeImmutableReleaseGeneration separately refuses to overwrite an already-recorded release-generation.json with a plan whose release_generation digest differs (ImmutableReleaseConflictError), covering the case where the drift is caught only after the first write.

release/contracts/release-generation.v1.schema.json documents the emitted evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json shape (additionalProperties:false, matching the convention already used by release/evidence/release-evidence.v1.schema.json, not modified here).

Pre-existing, found and reused but NOT modified (all outside this task's allowed scope, per this task's owner instructions): scripts/release/orchestrate-release.mjs + release/contracts/pipeline.v1.json + release/contracts/platforms.v1.json + tests/release/release-pipeline.test.mjs (a prior, non-book-mode 'feat(release): add source-only platform orchestration contract' commit 9297de3d/48bf821c -- a single-target manifest validator/plan-printer; this task's multi-platform-release.mjs is the layer that orchestrates across ALL targets and binds them to one commit, which that single-target validator does not do); scripts/release/verify-release-evidence.mjs + release/evidence/release-evidence.v1.schema.json (commit 98233f35 -- the later, per-target evidence-manifest layer MBR-807 depends on this task for); scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs and scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs (MBR-901/MBR-902's real platform verification, imported by sealed-platforms.mjs, never duplicated).

No cargo, pnpm, Tauri, right-release, codesign, notarytool, stapler, spctl, signtool, or AzureSignTool command was run at any point. No mutating git command (add/commit/checkout/stash/reset/rebase/push) was run. Only node --test scripts/release/pipeline/pipeline.test.mjs was executed -- see commands.log. No .github/workflows/**, CI, or hosted/self-hosted runner configuration was added, per this task's explicit owner override (MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md, MBR-903/R51).
